resources.string: Send direct traffic through the bundled ByeDPI (local DPI circumvention, no server needed)
One per line. "example.com" matches the domain and its subdomains; V2Ray syntax like "full:", "regexp:", "geosite:" is also accepted.
Raw byedpi (ciadpi) command line options. --ip, --port and --protect-path are managed by Guise. Leave empty to restore the default: -d1 -r1+s
Creates a profile that sends all proxied traffic through ByeDPI, so Guise can run without a proxy server
ByeDPI profile added to the current group
Try ByeDPI strategies against a few sites and pick one that works on this network
Find ByeDPI arguments that get through on the current network

Starts a temporary ByeDPI for each strategy and requests small files from the selected targets directly over the phone\'s current network (Wi-Fi / mobile data). Pick targets that are blocked by SNI/DPI rather than by IP (e.g. X, Twitch) — desync cannot help with IP blocks. Testing through a proxy node is not supported, so results only describe the network you are on now. Tap a result to apply or copy its arguments.
Targets: %1$s\nStrategies: %2$d · %3$d requests per target · timeout %4$ds · %5$d in parallel
One byedpi command line per line. Lines starting with # are ignored; {sni} is replaced with the fake SNI.
%1$s\n\nThis replaces the ByeDPI arguments in Settings and reloads the service if it is running.
ByeDPI is currently off: enable it in Settings or use the ByeDPI-only profile.
One domain or URL per line. A domain is tested as https://domain/; use a URL to a small file for more reliable results.
SNI/DPI-blocked in CN, IP usually reachable
Usually IP-blocked in CN: desync rarely helps
Blocked sites are usually DNS-poisoned too. With this on, the test resolves targets with the same DoH servers (and route) that Guise uses for ByeDPI traffic, falling back to system DNS if they fail.

Encrypted DNS used for names that go through ByeDPI (ByeDPI-only profile, \"selected domains\", and \"all direct traffic\" with route mode Direct), so blocked sites resolve to real addresses instead of poisoned ones. One per line. Prefer DoH to IP addresses, e.g. https://1.1.1.1/dns-query
Route the DoH queries above through ByeDPI (helps when the DoH server itself is filtered). Off: connect directly
Split connections across Wi-Fi and mobile data

Keeps mobile data connected while on Wi-Fi and spreads new connections to the proxy server over both. Only works with a remote proxy profile (SS, VMess, VLESS, Trojan, Hysteria2…); with the ByeDPI-only profile traffic stays on one network. Uses mobile data even on Wi-Fi and drains more battery.
Sample every N KB sent per network (auto mode)

Auto mode measures the real proxy connections (kernel RTT, jitter, retransmissions) — no extra probe traffic. One sample is taken every time this much has been sent over a network; no traffic, no sampling. Default 256.
Single network for ByeDPI / direct traffic
Not running (start Guise with this option on)

Only applies when an upload speed is set (Brutal congestion control). Normally Brutal raises its send rate by 1/(1 − loss) (up to 1.25×) to make up for lost packets; with this on it sends exactly the configured upload rate. Gentler on lossy or policed links.
UDP probe minimum interval (seconds, auto mode)

UDP/QUIC profiles (Hysteria2, TUIC, Juicity, mKCP…) can\'t be measured passively, so while traffic flows Guise sends one small probe to the server over each network (QUIC version negotiation, falling back to a TCP connect). At most one round per this many seconds, and only after the sample-trigger amount of traffic. 0 = off. Default 10.
